Question: Why does the resurrection matter if Jesus already died for sins?
ShortAnswer: The resurrection matters because without it, the cross would be just another death. Paul says it plainly: 'If Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins' (1 Corinthians 15:17).
DetailedAnswer: It is tempting to think the cross did all the work and the resurrection was a bonus — but the New Testament treats them as one saving event. First, the resurrection vindicates Jesus: it proves His claims were true and His sacrifice was accepted. Paul says Jesus 'was delivered over to death for our sins and was raised to life for our justification' (Romans 4:25) — the resurrection is God's 'Amen' to the cross. Second, it defeats death itself: Jesus did not just die for us, He rose ahead of us, as 'the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep' (1 Corinthians 15:20), guaranteeing our own resurrection. Third, it gives us new life now: 'just as Christ was raised from the dead... we too may live a new life' (Romans 6:4). A dead savior cannot intercede, cannot reign, and cannot return — but a risen Savior does all three: He lives to pray for us (Hebrews 7:25), He rules as King, and He will come again. That is why Peter calls the resurrection the source of 'a living hope' (1 Peter 1:3): because Jesus is alive, forgiveness is real, death is not the end, and the Christian life is powered by a living Lord, not a beautiful memory.
